text: The art of photography involves capturing images through the use of a camera. This process entails taking in the world around us and conveying a certain meaning or emotion through the captured images. In photography, there are three main settings to consider: aperture, shutter speed, and ISO. Aperture is the diameter of the lens opening, which affects the amount of light entering the camera. Larger apertures allow more light in, and thus photographers often opt for wider apertures in low-light conditions. The shutter speed, which is the time the sensor is exposed to light, is closely associated with the frame rate, which refers to the speed at which the camera's sensor captures images. While the shutter speed controls the length of time the sensor is exposed to light, aperture controls the amount of light that enters the camera.
